name: עִירָם
summary: Iram is the last named of the chiefs of Edom, after Magdiel (Gen 36:43; 1Ch 1:54). The list gives the chiefs “according to their dwellings in the land of their possession”, so the names are tied to settled places, and this one is עִיר with the ending ‑ām. Scripture does not explain it, and the reading “of a city” rests on the spelling and that setting only.

evidence.note: אַלּוּף מַגְדִּיאֵל אַלּוּף עִירָם: the chiefs of Edom לְמֹשְׁבֹתָם, “according to their dwellings”.
The same two chiefs close the list.
The same letters as the noun with a suffix: שַׁעַר עִירָם, “the gate of their city”.

note: BDB key p.cn.ag gathers five tokens: two of the chief (Gen 36:43; 1Ch 1:54) and three of עִירָם “their city” (Gen 34:20 twice; Deu 13:14) filed by spelling. The tie to עִיר is the weakest of the four names drafted: spelling only. The Septuagint spells it Ηραμ.
